name.text: Calculating coordinates of a point on a unit circle.

questiontext.text:
Let \(P\) be the point where the terminal side of the angle \(\theta={@theta@}\) intersects the unit circle.

What are the coordinates \((x,y)\) of point \(P\)?

Enter your answer as an ordered pair.

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]][[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
For a point \(P=(x,y)\) on the unit circle, the coordinates are determined by the angle \(\theta\):

\(x=\cos(\theta), \qquad y=\sin(\theta).\)

Therefore, the coordinates of \(P\) are

\(P=(\cos(\theta),\sin(\theta)).\)

To find the exact values, identify the reference angle and the quadrant in which \(\theta\) lies. The reference angle determines the magnitudes of the coordinates, while the quadrant determines their signs.

For example, if \(\theta=\frac{5\pi}{6}\), the reference angle is \(\frac{\pi}{6}\) and the angle lies in Quadrant II. Thus \(x\) is negative and \(y\) is positive:

\(x=-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}, \qquad y=\frac12.\)

Hence

\(P=\left(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2},\frac12\right).\)

prtcorrect.text: Correct answer, well done.

prtpartiallycorrect.text: Your answer is partially correct.

prtincorrect.text: Incorrect answer.

The angle selected for this question is \( \theta={@theta@}. \) For this angle, the corresponding point on the unit circle is \( (x_0,y_0)=({@x0@},{@y0@}). \)

Therefore, the correct coordinate pair is \( \boxed{[{@x0@},{@y0@}]}. \)

Your answer has the opposite sign for the \(x\)-coordinate: \( [{@-x0@},{@y0@}]. \) This means that you have selected the point on the opposite side of the \(y\)-axis.

Remember: the \(x\)-coordinate is negative on the left-hand side of the coordinate plane and positive on the right-hand side.

For the angle \( \theta={@theta@}, \) the point lies in the quadrant where \(x={@x0@}\) and \(y={@y0@}\). Hence, \( \boxed{[{@x0@},{@y0@}]} \) is the required answer.
